content:
alex: FYI: ACME reported their nightly embeddings job started returning a lot of 429s around 02:00UTC. They say nothing changed on their side besides a bigger dataset. Logs show repeated "rate_limit_exceeded" and occasional "dimension_mismatch".

maria: Can you paste a sample request/headers and the exact error payload? Need request_id and model name to trace routing.

alex: Pasting anonymized snippet: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer redacted
X-Client-Request-Id: acme-job-2026-02-14
Payload: {"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":[...40000 vectors...],"batch_size":2048}

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":{"message":"rate_limit_exceeded","type":"rate_limit"}}
```
Also got a couple of these: 
```
{"error":{"message":"embedding dimension mismatch: got 1536 expected 768"}}
```
They say they started parallelizing job into 8 workers after last week.

jordan: Looks like two issues: 1) sustained concurrency + large batch sizes -> hitting per-account burst and sustained rate limits; 2) dimension mismatch suggests mixing two model variants (maybe they rotated from 3-small to 3-large mid-run).

kai: Asked customer if they changed model mid-run? If clients rotate models while writing to same downstream store, dimension mismatch is expected. Also the SDK should fail fast for dimension mismatch.

alex: Customer confirms one of their workers was using an old config with text-embedding-3-small. They updated to large now. For 429s they say job was queued/retied aggressively.

maria: Recommended immediate mitigation to customer: 1) stop the job, 2) consolidate to single model variant, 3) reduce parallel workers to 2, 4) set batch_size to 256-512 and add exponential backoff with jitter on 429/5xx. Sent sample pseudo-code: 
```python
# backoff pseudo
for attempt in range(0,6):
    try: call_embeddings()
    except RateLimitError as e:
        sleep((2**attempt) * 0.1 + random.uniform(0,0.2))
```

lee: I'm going to open an internal request for a temporary ratecap lift (2h) while they rerun with safer config. Filing ticket now.

incidents-bot: Created internal ticket INF-1247 for "support: ACME embeddings 429 surge — temp ratecap lift request" by lee.

support-bot: Customer ticket CS-8871 opened. Notified ACME support contact with recommended mitigations and asked for a new run log after config change.

jordan: For long-term: ops should evaluate adding a per-account gradual throttling window instead of immediate hard burst drop — many customers do fanout of workers which triggers sudden spikes. Also update our SDK docs to recommend default batch_size 256 and built-in retry with jitter.

kai: Can infra check if the 429s were coming from the same routing pool or multiple? If multiple pools, might be global capacity pressure. alex, can you DM me the request ids?

alex: Sent the list to you via DM (acme-job-2026-02-14 with request ids). Initial look suggests all routed to us-west-2 pool node group A.

lee: Infra replied on INF-1247: temporary soft-limits increased for account acme-corp by +50% for 2 hours. Also they enabled extra queueing for embeddings in pool A.

maria: Customer reran with one model, batch_size 512, concurrency 2, and applied backoff. They reported 0 429s in the second run and dims are consistent. They still want guidance to avoid future incidents.

jordan: Action items: 1) docs PR to add embedding bulk best-practices (batch size, concurrency, retries) — assignee: jordan, due EOD +3; 2) SDK: default retry with decorrelated jitter and a max concurrency guard — assignee: devex (kai) +1 sprint; 3) infra: investigate pool-level throttling behavior and consider smoothing algorithm — assignee: eng-infra (lee) +2 weeks.

alex: Closing thread for now, will update CS-8871 with resolution steps and link to docs when PR is merged. :white_check_mark:
